newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher in high volume.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher in high volume.

text.p: Israeli CPI-linked and unlinked bonds closed slightly higher on Wednesday in mixed and active trading while dollar-linked bonds ended lower, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.02 pct to 170.36.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.01 pct to 160.93
Volume was high at 243 million shekels with most of the activity concentrated in unlinked bonds and Makams.

"Trading was very mixed today and the market was stable. Most of the activity was in unlinked bonds as they offer very nice yields. In the inflation-linked bonds we saw some profit- taking," said Elisha Rosenfeld at Lehave Securities.
"CPI-linked long bonds were rising today by 0.08 to 0.13 percent. The short and medium-term bonds rose only mildly," said Roy Meir at Simodan.

"Activty in the unlinked bonds was very high with volume of 90 million shekels. The mutual funds were selling bonds while investors were buying them because they offer high yields as inflation is expected to fall sharply," Meir added.
Traders noted that the December consumer price index is expected to be relativly low, around 0.5 percent.
"With falling inflation and high interest rates, the unlinked bonds and Makams are very attractive. Those bonds are believed to offer real yields of around nine percent," Rosenfeld said.

Traders said that the dollar-linked bonds closed lower following the rise of the shekel against the dollar on Tuesday. Meir added that dollar-linked bonds would probably rise on Thursday following the rise of the dollar today.
On Wednesday the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2520 shekels against 3.2420 on Tuesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
